state.context: Daily Ten is an offline-first mobile home-workout PWA. Evaluate only the supplied implementation evidence. The user explicitly accepts judging demo form themselves; external coach review is not a release criterion. Full-motion demo coverage and in-app usability still matter.
state.movement: Four distinct AI-generated 16-frame local sprite sheets show standard push-up, controlled squat, glute bridge and seated resistance-band row anchored under both feet. They can play, pause, slow, scrub and replay. Exact-name mapping covers 11 of 73 programmed names; 62 names have no in-app motion, and complete real video count is 0. Old stick figures are hidden.
state.help: During workouts, in-app help pauses the timer, keeps the current exercise and remaining time, hides the external YouTube link, and returns to the same place. Reload restores a paused checkpoint. Missing-motion exercises can be skipped in the modal without losing the workout or awarding completion. Focused browser tests pass. iOS eviction is unverified.
state.timing: Workout duration is computed from repetitions times tempo, holds, rest, preparation and transitions across levels and equipment options. Controlled squat sprite is paced approximately 3 seconds down and 1 second up. Workout prescription remains developer-defined, without individualized calibration.
state.program: Weekly split has two push days, two lower-body exposures, two pull exposures with overlap, one recovery day and Boss day. Band rows use feet rather than fixed home anchors. No-band upper-back substitutes are explicitly low-resistance. Rep, exertion, posture and pain feedback plus recent movement-pattern evidence gate manual progression. No automatic weekly volume adjustment.
state.navigation: Today offers the next action; workout shows current, next, progress, help, pause, skip and exit. Movement library marks exercises with 16-frame demos. A 375x667 browser screenshot shows clear pose and controls. There has been no independent user study. Full regression test is running; focused in-app demo test passed.
